title: Trump Truth Social / DJT Stock SPAC Merger (March 22, 2024)
description_short: Trump Truth Social / DJT Stock SPAC Merger (March 22, 2024)
description_medium: The record says Trump Media & Technology Group completed a SPAC merger on March 22, 2024, and places Donald Trump’s stake at $3–4 billion on paper. It also alleges insider enrichment and market manipulation. The only linked Reuters story concerns Trump’s hush-money trial, so it does not document the merger, shareholding, valuation basis, or alleged conduct.
description_long: The record says Trump Media & Technology Group completed a merger with a special-purpose acquisition company on March 22, 2024, and puts Donald Trump’s stake at a paper value of $3–4 billion. It also characterizes the stock as detached from the company’s fundamentals and alleges insider enrichment and market manipulation. Those claims are not established by the only linked Reuters story, which concerns Trump’s New York hush-money trial. The assignment includes no merger-closing filing, shareholding record, contemporaneous share price, or calculation explaining the stated valuation. A paper value is not the same as money received by Trump. The packet also includes no enforcement action or other specific evidence supporting manipulation or insider enrichment. The linked article cannot resolve these gaps, so no finding of fraud or manipulation is stated here. To complete the record, provide a source documenting the merger and Trump’s shareholding and valuation basis at the relevant date. Any claim of manipulation or insider enrichment requires specific supporting evidence, such as a relevant investigation or enforcement record; volatility or a high market price alone would not establish it.
notes: The existing Reuters link is about the hush-money trial and cannot resolve this entry’s missing evidence, so no read of it would answer the blocker. The assignment supplies no merger-closing record, Trump share count and valuation calculation as of March 22, 2024, or specific evidence for the insider-enrichment and market-manipulation allegations. The $3–4 billion figure must remain attributed as an unverified paper valuation, not realized proceeds.
proposed_correction: Add an existing source documenting the merger, Trump’s shareholding and valuation basis; remove the manipulation and insider-enrichment claims unless specific evidence supports them.

title: EPA Proposed Repealing the Clean Power Plan in 2017
description_short: EPA Proposed Repealing the Clean Power Plan in 2017
description_medium: On October 10, 2017, EPA Administrator Scott Pruitt announced that the Trump administration would propose repealing the Obama-era Clean Power Plan. EPA’s October 16 Federal Register notice formally opened the rulemaking and argued that the agency lacked authority for the plan. This was a proposal, not an immediate repeal; the linked notice does not establish the policy’s eventual legal outcome or any resulting emissions change.
description_long: On October 10, 2017, EPA Administrator Scott Pruitt announced that the administration intended to propose repealing the Clean Power Plan, which set carbon-pollution guidelines for existing power plants. The EPA notice published on October 16 formalized the proposed repeal and set out the agency’s legal view that the plan exceeded its statutory authority. Pruitt publicly framed the announcement as the end of the “war on coal.” At that point, the action was a rulemaking proposal, not a final repeal, so existing requirements were not immediately removed by the announcement. The measure addressed carbon emissions from power plants, but this record does not claim a specific emissions result or quantify effects for the fossil-fuel industry. The linked Federal Register notice supports the proposal and the agency’s stated legal rationale. Establishing the final regulatory or court outcome would require later records. The prior headline and summary described the proposal as a completed rollback, so this version changes the title and narrative to match the dated primary source.
notes: The focused read reached the Federal Register automated-access page, while the assignment’s linked-source metadata and existing account identify the October 16, 2017 notice as a proposed repeal with EPA’s stated legal rationale. The title and descriptions now stop at that supported procedural step; the final rule and court outcome are not claimed.
